newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador's Banco Guayaquil to merge with Sociedad.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador's Banco Guayaquil to merge with Sociedad.

text.p: Ecuador's Banco de Guayaquil said Friday it had agreed to merge with Banco Sociedad General under a share-exchange that would make it the nation's sixth largest bank in terms of assets.
The institution would be called Banco de Guayaquil after the current bank of that name, now seventh in ranking, absorbs Sociedad General, now 21st among Ecuador's financial institutions.
"Two of the oldest and most prestigious banks in the country...have signed a share swap agreement designed to begin a merger process," Guayaquil said in a statement.
The banks will continue to operate independently until the merger is completed in four to six months, a Banco de Guayaquil executive said in an interview.
Shareholders of Banco Sociedad General, largely held by the Maspons family, will receive 15 percent of the total shares of the merged association.
The Maspons family is one of the richest in Guayaquil, 420 kilometers south of Quito.
The new merged bank will be Ecuador's fifth in terms of deposits. The merger must be approved by the superintendent of banks.
The statement said after including Sociedad General's assets of 455,238 million sucres ($123.8 million), the new entity's assets will be 2.21 billion sucres ($603 million).
Their total deposits will be 923,640 million sucres ($251.2 million).
